chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Razi from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Rifa'ah ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Cooperate in eating the pre-dawn meal (suhur) for the sake of fasting during the day, and in sleeping during the midday rest (qaylulah) for the sake of standing in prayer during the night."

key_terms.قِيَامِ اللَّيْلِ: Night prayer or standing in prayer during the night

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of sleeping during the midday rest (qaylulah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith elucidates the Prophetic wisdom behind balancing physical sustenance with spiritual devotion, framing the midday nap (qaylulah) not as laziness but as a strategic preparation for night worship. Shia scholars emphasize this dual mechanism of 'cooperation' (ta'awun) between bodily needs and ritual acts, illustrating how the body serves as a vessel for enhanced khushu' in qiyam al-layl.
